Managing Normal 
Discomforts in 3 Slides
NRBS 3410 
Summer 2026

Managing Discomforts of Pregnancy
• Urinary frequency
• Pelvic floor exercises (kegel)
• Empty bladder with first sensation 
• Avoid caffeine
• Reduce after-dinner fluid
• Fatigue
• Attempt to get 8 hours of sleep
• Eat healthy balanced diet
• Schedule afternoon nap
• Rest whenever you feel tired
• Nausea & Vomiting
• Avoid empty stomach: carry healthy 
snacks (granola/enery bar)
• Eat dry crackers in bed before rising
• Eat several small meals throughout day
• Avoid brushing teeth immediately after 
eating (gag reflex)
• Acupressure wristband
• Drink fluids between meals not with
• Avoid greasy, fried foods or food with 
strong odors

Managing Discomforts #2
• Backache
• Avoid standing or sitting in one 
position for too long
• Heating pad on low setting
• Support lower back with pillows 
when sitting
• Use proper body alignment lifting
• Avoid excessive bending, lifting 
walking without rest periods
• Wear supportive low-heels
• Stand shoulders back for alignment
• Leg Cramps
• Elevate legs above heart throughout day
• If you get cramp, straighten both legs and flex 
feet toward body
• Ask provider about additional calcium to 
prevent 
• Varicose veins
• Walk daily to improve leg circulation
• Elevate legs when resting
• Avoid standing for long periods
• Avoid constrictive clothing Don’t cross legs 
when sitting
• Support stockings if comfortable

Managing Discomforts #3
• Hemorrhoids
• Establish regular time for bowel movement
• Avoid constipation and straining
• Prevent straining by drinking plenty of fluid
• Warm sitz bath and witch hazel pads
• Constipation
• Increase high fiber foods and drink eight 8oz 
water day
• Prunes or prune juice
• Warm liquids upon rising
• Exercise daily
• Reduce cheese consumption
• Heartburn
• Avoid spicy/greasy food
• Sleep on several pillows (30 degrees)
• Avoid caffeine
• No smoking
• Sit upright for 3 hours after eating
• Drink sips of water to reduce burning
• Keep food diary to avoid trigger foods (soda, 
chocolate, fried food, citrus)
• Take tums as directed by provider
• Braxton Hicks Contractions
• Drink more fluids
• These are normal, change position to decrease the 
awareness of sensation
